## 2024-06-03 - [DOMPurify for DangerouslySetInnerHTML]
**Vulnerability:** Several components use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to render strings representing fuzzy search matches or similar UI highlights. The inputs passed to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` are generated by surrounding parts of the user input with spans, without first sanitizing the user input.
**Learning:** `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is used in many model pickers and `HistoryView.tsx` to highlight text matches. While these inputs might come from internal state or API responses, they are ultimately user-controllable or external data (model names, prompt history) and can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
**Prevention:** Always use `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)` when using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to sanitize the string and strip any malicious HTML tags/scripts, or properly escape HTML entities in strings before wrapping matched sub-strings in tags.
